summary: An excerpt from a fiction novel (Book 10, part 97) set around CogRad, a company building networked repeater arrays on Native American reservations. MacDiarmid confronts Lee-Daniel, who is angry at being pushed aside; MacDiarmid praises his work but says the company is moving abroad and needs a different touch. The passage then describes resistance from Paiute elders at the Moapa River reservation, who refuse survey access to a burial ground, and a briefing by a self-described Akwesasne Warrior named Meatloaf about restricted zones marked on a topo map.
one_line: In a fiction excerpt, CogRad founder MacDiarmid pushes out Lee-Daniel, while surveyors face Paiute and Warrior resistance to reservation repeater sites.
key_facts: MacDiarmid tells Lee-Daniel he owns fifteen percent of CogRad, the same stake as Lee-Daniel.
Lee-Daniel apologizes to MacDiarmid and asks him to sit down and explain, saying 'Please.'
MacDiarmid says Lee-Daniel has done excellent work and that the company is moving into a new phase that needs a delicate touch.
MacDiarmid says that if Canada ends up in a firefight, 'what'll it be like in Guatemala?'
The Paiute elders at the Moapa River Indian Reservation refuse CogRad's surveyor crew access to a burial ground that would have made a good repeater-array site.
The Paiute elders were tempted by a share of every casino's action from offering secure connectivity for phones and data.
A man called 'Meatloaf,' wearing camou fatigues with pow-wow badges, gives a two-hour briefing in the school auditorium.
Meatloaf says areas marked with post-its are strategic and that no one except a Warrior may go within 20 meters, which Lee-Daniel translates as sixty feet.
The briefing takes place in the fading light of the sun streaming through steel-reinforced windows.
Lee-Daniel's surveyors and antennamen are described as products of the American educational system, impedance-mismatched with the metric-speaking world.
